issues.main_description_html:
• The support menu should appear only for the support role

RESULT

Branch: fix/651-support-menu-sidebar · Commit: a52ae17

What was actually wrong

The opposite of the title: Support was not leaking onto Profile, it was missing everywhere else. hasSupportAccess and accountNavItemsFor were already correct and are untouched — the sidebar simply was not always told who is signed in.

Caller What it passed Result for a support user
AccountShell.tsx:58 (Profile, Billing, Help…) email + role from the user store Support shown ✅
app/dashboard/page.tsx:66 nothing — <DashboardSidebar /> accountNavItemsFor({}) filtered it out ❌

Same session, same role, two different menus. The dashboard already had user in scope from useDashboard(); it just never handed it to the sidebar.

Fix

DashboardSidebar reads the shared user record itself (useUserStore), keeping the props as an override for callers that already hold it — one guard inside the component instead of a prop threaded through every caller, so the next page that renders a bare sidebar cannot reintroduce it.

Files: src/components/dashboard/DashboardSidebar.tsx, src/components/dashboard/__tests__/DashboardSidebar.test.tsx (new).

Checks

tsc --noEmit pass · eslint pass · vitest 138 files, 1104 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed — 5 new tests: role from the store with no props, non-support role hidden, signed-out hidden, explicit prop honoured, shared destinations intact. The first was confirmed to fail without the fix, so it is not a vacuous test.

Worth a follow-up

This fix is right regardless of role data, but it was never confirmed that the account in the screenshot actually holds the support role. If it does not, something upstream is granting it — a separate and security-relevant question.

issues.display_title: Issue #652: Handle Issue Description is Short, but there is a “Show More” toggle
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT

Branch: fix/652-show-more-only-when-clamped · Commit: d1b1612

Cause

PreviewInfoCard.tsx:154 rendered the toggle for every description that existed. The paragraph carries line-clamp-3, but nothing ever asked whether the clamp actually bit — so a one-line note like "ruang tester" got a Show More that expands one line into the same one line.

Fix

The card measures it: a ref on the paragraph, scrollHeight > clientHeight while the clamp is on, re-measured through a ResizeObserver because the same text clamps at one card width and not at another. The toggle renders only when the text is genuinely cut off.

Length of the string would not do — three lines is a CSS clamp, and whether the text reaches it depends on the card width and the font, so only the browser knows.

The button also stays while the description is expanded: once unclamped nothing overflows, and dropping it there would strand the reader with no way back.

Files: src/components/editor/preview/PreviewInfoCard.tsx, src/components/editor/preview/__tests__/PreviewInfoCard.test.tsx.

Checks

tsc --noEmit pass · eslint pass · vitest 138 files, 1106 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed.

Two new tests: a description that already fits renders no toggle, and Show Less survives expansion. jsdom lays nothing out (scrollHeight === clientHeight === 0) and has no ResizeObserver, so the tests stub the two heights and the component skips the observer when it is absent — which covers SSR as well. The first new test was confirmed to fail without the fix.

issues.display_title: Issue #672: Editor Map: floor stack snap for Selected Floor placement (PRD #594)
issues.main_description_html:
Stacking a multi-floor building in Editor Map mode is trial and error. Selected Floor placement already writes level.mapTransform.offsetX/offsetY from both drag (src/lib/map/useBuildingDrag.ts:107-117) and the nudge D-pad (src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx:238-246), but nothing helps the creator land a floor on the one below it — a six-floor building can ship one floor visibly off.

PRD #594 asks for a Snap mode on Selected Floor placement: with snap on, moving the active floor aligns it to another floor in the same building once it comes within tolerance, by footprint center or footprint edge. Snap writes offset only — never rotation, never scale.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What already holds (no code needed)

Validated against the code before scoping — six of the PRD's twelve acceptance criteria are already true:

PRD AC Why it already holds
Applies only in Selected Floor scope Snap sits inside the existing scope === "floor" branches; every other scope is a different branch
Writes only the active floor offset patchLevelTransform (src/lib/map/placement.ts:15) takes a patch object that is literally { offsetX, offsetY }
Never changes rotationDeg / scale same patch object
Siblings, building and project transforms do not move covered by src/lib/map/__tests__/placement.test.ts:61-66; the building pivot buildingBBoxCenter (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:182) is computed from untransformed level centers, so a floor offset provably cannot move the building frame
Save/reload preserves alignment mapTransform lives inside canvasData, autosaved at 2 s
Inert in outdoor mode Editor Map has no outdoor mode. useAutoOutdoor has one caller, PreviewOverlay.tsx, which mounts only under previewMode. Editor3DMapView imports useOutdoorLayer — a layer, not a mode. The comment at MapTransformControl.tsx:333-336 claiming otherwise is stale and should be corrected in this task

The snap arithmetic is also far smaller than it looks: makeLevelLocalTransform (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:151) rotates and scales about the level's own bbox center, so a level's placed center is exactly levelBBoxCenter(level) + (offsetX, offsetY) no matter how it is rotated or scaled — pinned today by geojson-level-transform.test.ts:49-56. Candidates in the same building share every frame above them, so the whole calculation is subtraction in local model px. No lng/lat, no frame composition, no new geometry code: levelBBox and levelBBoxCenter already exist and only need exporting.

Scope

  • src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts — export levelBBox (:131) and levelBBoxCenter (:145)
  • src/lib/map/placement.ts — snapFloorOffset(cd, levelId, offsetX, offsetY, tol) returning { offsetX, offsetY, snappedTo }, plus moveLevelByMapStep(...), the shared point drag and nudge both route through. They have no shared commit path today; patchLevelTransform is not one, since it also carries rotation-only and scale-only patches
  • src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts — floorStackSnapEnabled: boolean + setter, following mapMoveMode (:24, :136, :205). Session-only by construction: nothing persists unless hand-copied into buildPersistedState (src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:50)
  • src/lib/map/useBuildingDrag.ts — route the floor branch through the shared helper. The snap flag goes in a ref alongside the others (:60-72), never in the effect deps (:174) — a remount there commits an in-flight drag
  • src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx — same helper in handleNudge; Snap toggle in the popup beside Reset (:446-453), rendered only when floorScope (:299); fix the stale outdoor comment
  • src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx — pass the flag/tolerance into useBuildingDrag; append the matched floor to the existing move-mode hint (:356)
  • src/lib/map/__tests__/floorSnap.test.ts (new)

Out of scope: building-to-building snap, cross-building snap, rotation/scale snap, schema changes, preview and live viewer.

Decisions to make while building

  1. Tolerance must stay well under computeBBox span x 0.02. The nudge step is 2% of the whole-model span (MapTransformControl.tsx:233-235) and accumulates from current state, so a tolerance at or above one step traps the floor: every arrow click moves one step and snap pulls it straight back. Drag is immune — it recomputes from the pre-drag snapshot. Alternative if the margin is too tight: nudge snaps only on the click that enters tolerance.
  2. Candidate set. All same-building floors, or only the rendered ones? The editor draws levelsAtOrBelow (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLayer.ts:193), so snapping floor 2 to floor 5 jumps toward geometry that is not on screen. Restricting candidates to the rendered set is cheaper and self-explaining.

Deliberately trimmed from the PRD

  • No separate floorSnap.ts — placement.ts is already the shared home of every placement write, and is already unit-tested
  • Feedback is the text in the existing move-mode chip, not a MapLibre guide-line layer. Floors below already render as ghost geometry, so a snap is visibly an alignment; a guide line means a new source, a new layer, a style-reload re-add and teardown. Add one later only if beta users say they cannot tell
  • Four unit tests, not the PRD's twelve plus five component tests. "Rotation unchanged" and "scale unchanged" assert an object literal; "siblings do not move" is placement.test.ts:61-66; "drag and nudge behave the same" stops being a behaviour once both call one function. The component tests need the full store plus a fake MapLibre and would pin markup the design branch still churns
  • Edge snapping stays in, but as a Should, not a Must: same-building floors usually share a footprint, where edge and center land on the same point. It must not grow into per-corner or per-wall alignment

Acceptance

  • Snap toggle appears in the map transform popup, only under Selected Floor scope
  • Snap candidates are floors in the selected building; the active floor is excluded; floors with no usable footprint are skipped
  • Drag applies snap within tolerance; nudge applies the same snap and stays escapable
  • Center-to-center and left/right/top/bottom edge alignment both work
  • Snap writes only offsetX/offsetY; rotation and scale unchanged; siblings, building and project frames unchanged
  • With no eligible candidate, drag and nudge behave exactly as today
  • The matched floor is named in the move-mode hint while a snap is applied
  • Save and reload preserve the snapped alignment
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Source PRD: #594 (docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-10-floor-stack-snap-mode/prd.md, branch product-docs).

RESULT

Branch: feature/672-floor-stack-snap-prd (from development) · Commits: 2ed8ab4, 6064f75

PRD #594 implemented as written. Two versions were built and compared; this is the full PRD one. The scoped alternative (443 lines, text-only feedback, no separate helper module, four unit tests) sits on feature/672-floor-stack-snap and was not taken.

Snap

Selected Floor placement gets a Snap toggle. With it on, moving the active floor pulls it onto another floor of the same building once it comes within tolerance — footprint centre to centre, or matching edge to edge (left to left, right to right, top to top, bottom to bottom). Opposite edges are never paired. The two axes snap independently, so a floor can catch one edge while still moving freely along the other.

Candidate filtering, the alignment arithmetic and the guide geometry all live in one pure module, src/lib/map/floorSnap.ts, reached by drag and by the nudge D-pad through the same moveLevelByMapStep. That answers both risks the PRD names in §9: cross-building candidates cannot leak in, and drag and nudge cannot drift apart.

Tolerance, and why the arrows still work

Tolerance is 1% of the active floor's raw footprint span, overridable per call via options.tolerance.

Relative, because a fixed pixel count means nothing without the model's size — one that feels right on a shop is invisible on an airport.

Measured off the raw span because the pull has to stay escapable. The nudge D-pad steps 2% of the whole model's span and accumulates from the current offset, so a tolerance at or above one step would drag the floor back onto the target every click and trap it there. computeBBox spans every level's raw geometry, so one floor's raw span can never exceed the model's — 1% of a floor is always under 2% of the model, whatever that floor's rotation or scale. One arrow always out-steps the pull. Drag is immune anyway: it recomputes from the pre-drag snapshot every move, so the floor lets go the moment the cursor leaves tolerance.

Why the arithmetic is small

makeLevelLocalTransform rotates and scales a level about its own footprint centre, so a level's placed centre is exactly levelBBoxCenter + (offsetX, offsetY) no matter how it is turned — already pinned by geojson-level-transform.test.ts:49-56. Same-building candidates share every frame above them, so no frame composition is needed and the whole calculation is subtraction in building-frame model px.

Only offsetX/offsetY are ever written. Rotation and scale are read, because they change the box a floor presents, and never written. Sibling floors keep object identity, and the building pivot buildingBBoxCenter is computed from untransformed level centres — so a floor offset provably cannot move the building or project frame.

Feedback

A dashed guide on each matched axis, spanning both footprints, plus the matched floor's name in the move-mode hint. The guides are drawn in the building frame — via a new makeBuildingFramePixelTransform — not the active floor's own, which is the thing being aligned: projecting through it would drag the guide along with the floor instead of leaving it on the target. Both cues clear when the match goes, when the gesture ends, when Snap is switched off, and when the floor, building or scope changes.

The transient match lives in the store rather than local state because nudge is raised in MapTransformControl while the guide is drawn from Editor3DMapView. It is never persisted — the persist allowlist in wizardState.ts is hand-written, so anything not copied there is session-only by construction.

Control placement

The toggle sits in the map transform popup, shown in every scope but inert outside Selected Floor rather than hidden. A control that disappears when the scope changes reads as a bug, and the disabled tooltip is where the rule gets taught — PRD §9's first risk is "users may not realize snap applies only to Active Floor scope". With no eligible floor in the building the toggle still works and the tooltip says why, so there is no dead end.

Performance

Snap asks every candidate floor for its bounding box on every mousemove, and finding one tessellates each curved wall. Measured on a six-floor building of 300 bezier walls each: 7.344 ms per mousemove, past the frame budget before MapLibre had drawn anything.

levelBBox now caches on the geometry object. A level is re-created on every placement write while its layout is carried across untouched, so keying there survives a drag and still misses when the geometry is really edited — nothing mutates a layout in place, every writer builds a fresh one. Same move now costs 0.049 ms.

Separately, location was a fresh { lat, lng } literal per render and sits in useFloorPlanLayer's dependency list, so any unrelated re-render of the map view rebuilt and re-pushed the whole model's GeoJSON. Memoized.

R14 — outdoor mode

Satisfied vacuously, with no code. Editor Map mode has no outdoor state: useAutoOutdoor has one caller, PreviewOverlay, which mounts only under previewMode; Editor3DMapView imports useOutdoorLayer, which is a context-shell layer, not a mode. The Overview state was removed from Editor Map by #591 R1-R6. A stale comment in MapTransformControl.tsx claiming these controls guarded against it has been dropped. The PRD's manual-QA item "confirm outdoor mode prevents snap placement edits" is not executable in Editor Map.

issues.display_title: Issue #673: Mappedin import: floors arrive in the export's arbitrary order — sort each floor stack by floors.geojson elevation
issues.main_description_html:
Fixes the report in #628: a Mappedin import lands in the project in an order that is not the order the file describes.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Asset: the reporter's own export — Multi-Family Hi-Rise Demo, 36 floors, one floor stack (.playwright-mcp/demo/628/mappedin-hi-rise-36-floors.zip)

Evidence

.playwright-mcp/demo/628/video-628-floor-order.mp4 — the same file imported twice, development on the left half of the run and the fix on the right, read straight out of the review modal:

BEFORE  Level 1 | Mezzanine | Level 2 | Level 3 | Level 4 | RA | Level 24 | Level 17 | …
        …ending: Level 34 | PH | Level 18 | Level 16     ← badge "1" = the ground floor
AFTER   RA | PH | Level 34 | Level 33 | … | Level 2 | Mezzanine | Level 1

The BEFORE line is byte-for-byte the level dropdown in #628's screenshot. The AFTER line is byte-for-byte the Mappedin reference viewer beside it.

Root cause

src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts:76 and :87:

let floorIds = floorStacks.flatMap((stack) => stack.floors ?? []);
// "Do NOT sort by floors.geojson `elevation`: it's an entry-floor ordinal … not a physical height."
floorIds.reverse();

The parser assumes floor-stacks.json lists floors top-first and reverses it. It does not list them in any physical order at all. In the reporter's file the stack reads Level 1, Mezzanine, Level 2, Level 3, Level 4, RA, Level 24, Level 17, Level 8, Level 19, Level 33, … — neither ascending nor descending — so reversing it produces a reversed scramble, which is exactly what shipped.

reverse() survived #369 because every sample available then was 1–2 floors, where reversing and sorting are indistinguishable (Airport Demo: Level 2 elevation 0, Level 1 elevation −1).

The real order is floors.geojson elevation, which the file carries on 100% of features and which the current FloorsGeoJson type does not even read. Per the MVF v3 spec it is required, an integer ordinal, 0 = ground, negatives below grade, and unique within a floor stack rather than within the file. Mappedin's own Web SDK sorts its level selector by it. The #369 comment's premise ("not a physical height") is true; its conclusion ("not a sort key") is false, and it is self-refuting — −1 < 0 puts Airport's Level 1 below Level 2, which is right.

Fix

Order each stack by its own elevation, ascending, which is the app's canvasData.levels contract (bottom→top, levelBaseHeights).

Per stack, not globally — elevation is only unique inside one stack, so a global sort over the flattened list interleaves buildings and breaks the invariant documented at src/lib/mappedin/types.ts:86. floorIds is now derived from buildings.flatMap(...), so the two orders are structurally incapable of disagreeing, and the per-stack .reverse() disappears with no replacement.

Missing or non-finite elevation falls back to the feature's own position in floors.geojson — not to 0, which would drop an unannotated floor next to the ground floor.

Files: src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts, src/lib/mappedin-import/extractFloors.ts (stale comment), src/lib/mappedin/__tests__/{fixtures,parse.test,sample-zip.int.test}.ts.

Tests

  • unscrambles a real 36-floor stack listed in arbitrary order — fixture built from the reporter's actual file order, verified byte-for-byte against the zip. Fails under reverse() and under any verbatim pass-through.
  • sorts the floors.geojson fallback when floor-stacks.json is missing
  • sorts each stack separately — elevation is unique per stack, not per file — two stacks with colliding 0..2; buildings must stay contiguous.
  • keeps floors.geojson order when the export carries no elevation
  • Fixtures gained elevation so the sort is actually exercised in CI — samples/ is gitignored, so the integration test skips there.

Acceptance

  • A multi-floor Mappedin import reaches the project in the order Mappedin itself shows.
  • Floors of a multi-building export stay contiguous per building; no interleaving.
  • An export with no elevation keeps its file order rather than being reversed.
  • Airport Demo (negative elevation) still imports Level 1 then Level 2.
  • tsc --noEmit, eslint, vitest green.

Manual verification

  1. New project → import mappedin-hi-rise-36-floors.zip.
  2. The review modal reads RA, PH, Level 34 … down to Mezzanine, Level 1.
  3. Continue to Editor → the floor selector shows the same order.
  4. Re-import a single-floor export and an image-only flow — both unchanged.

Out of scope

  • Projects already imported keep their scrambled order. src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts hydrates canvasData.levels verbatim and there is no migration; the reporter must re-import. Worth a release note.
  • Go backend divergence. Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO/src/utils/mappedin.go:348-357 appends stack.Floors verbatim and never reads elevation, so /v1/import/mappedin still returns the scrambled order. Nothing in src/ calls the proxy routes today, so nothing regresses — but the two parsers now disagree. Flagged per CLAUDE.md; needs its own BE task on Project #112.
  • src/lib/mappedin-editor (the .txt editor export) carries no floor or elevation signal at all, so it cannot exhibit this bug.

RESULT

Branch: fix/673-mappedin-floor-order · Commit: 1174be2 · 5 files, +120/−39 · merged into development as 7256f20

What changed

src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts now sorts each floor stack by its own floors.geojson elevation, ascending — the app's bottom→top canvasData.levels contract — instead of reversing the file's order. Both .reverse() calls are gone.

  • Per stack, not globally. MVF v3 scopes elevation uniqueness to the floorStack, so a global sort over the flattened list would interleave buildings. floorIds is now derived from buildings.flatMap((b) => b.floorIds), which makes ParsedFloor order and ParsedBuilding.floorIds structurally unable to disagree — the invariant documented at types.ts:86 is true by construction for the first time, and the per-stack reverse retires with no replacement.
  • Fallback is position, not zero. A missing or non-finite elevation keeps the feature's own index in floors.geojson; ?? 0 would strand an unannotated floor beside the ground floor. Only reachable for pre-v3 exports — elevation is required in v3 and present on 100% of features in all four real assets.
  • The #369 comments in parse.ts and extractFloors.ts were rewritten, not deleted, and cite the spec: the sort was introduced once before (1474ecd), reverted 28 minutes later (591b246), and replaced by reverse() ten minutes after that (2c3084f). The comment is why it stayed broken.

Verification against the reporter's own file

BEFORE  Level 1 | Mezzanine | Level 2 | Level 3 | Level 4 | RA | Level 24 | Level 17 | …
        …ending: Level 34 | PH | Level 18 | Level 16      ← badge "1" = the ground floor
AFTER   RA | PH | Level 34 | Level 33 | … | Level 2 | Mezzanine | Level 1

BEFORE is byte-for-byte the dropdown in #628's screenshot; AFTER is byte-for-byte the Mappedin reference viewer beside it. Frames: check-30.png (RA wedged between Level 4 and Level 24), check-44.png (before, "Level 16" as the ground floor), check-78.png (after, Level 1 at the bottom).

The same chain was run headlessly through parse → runImport → groupFloorsByBuilding → mergeImportIntoProject → buildFloorOptions, and against the pre-fix parse.ts to confirm the reproduction rather than assume it.

Checks

Four new tests in parse.test.ts, the decisive one built from the reporter's actual 36-floor file order (verified byte-for-byte against the zip) — it fails under reverse() and under any verbatim pass-through. Fixtures gained elevation, without which every fixture-driven test would have exercised only the fallback and the sort would have shipped with no CI coverage: samples/ is gitignored, so the integration test skips in CI.

Still open

  • Projects imported before this fix keep their scrambled order — persistence/wizardState.ts hydrates verbatim and there is no migration. The reporter must re-import. Release note needed.
  • The Go backend still appends stack.Floors verbatim (mappedin.go:348-357); needs its own task on Project #112.

issues.display_title: Issue #676: Access parent resolution: stamp the origin level on placement, so a lift drawn upstairs is not re-parented to its own copy
issues.main_description_html:
Closes the last gap in the Front End Developer TODO of #666 (PRD: door-based building connectors and Access parent-child controls). Everything else in that list shipped in 4282141; this is the one rule that did not survive contact with the authoring flow.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Design: #671 (closed) — no code on design/door-based-building-connectors; that branch still points at a8305ee, an old development.

The bug

Draw a Lift on Level 3, then set Downstairs = Level 2, Level 1. The moment the children appear, the object you drew stops being the parent:

  • the Level 3 card flips to the child card — "Managed by parent · Type and connected floors are set on Level 1"
  • Level 1 — a copy the editor generated seconds ago — inherits Type, Downstairs and Upstairs
  • View parent on the object the user authored navigates down to its own clone
  • in Map mode the Not linked badge moves to the generated copy, so the Information link is offered on the wrong marker (MapObjectMarkers.tsx:128, SelectedFeaturePanel.tsx)

Only groups that grow downward are visibly wrong. A parent on the ground floor connecting upward already sits first in level order, so the fallback happens to pick it — which is why this reads as correct in the common case and inverts in the multi-storey one the PRD is about.

Root cause

accessParent (src/lib/editor/access.ts:58) resolves in the PRD's documented order — stored origin → earliest createdAt → first member in stored level order.

Rule 1 is dead code for everything the editor creates. accessOriginLevelId is written in exactly one place, migrateLegacyAccess (access.ts:390), which only runs on pre-#585 projects. interactions.ts:181 places a new marker with neither field, and the bridge stamps createdAt only.

Rule 2 cannot break the tie. withAccessSpan clones the template verbatim — const copy = { ...template, id: makeId(), x, y } (access.ts:302) — so every generated child carries the parent's own createdAt. stamped.reduce((a, b) => b.createdAt < a.createdAt ? b : a) never sees a smaller value and keeps its seed.

So every group authored in the editor falls through to rule 3, the legacy last resort: first member in stored level order = the lowest floor.

createdAt is not the place to fix this — it is also the object list's sort key (#392, objectRows.ts:99), and dropping it from copies would sink them to the bottom of their floor's list.

Fix

Stamp accessOriginLevelId where createdAt is already stamped: modelToLevel in src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts, the single choke point every editor change flows through on its way to the store.

accessPoints: (model.access ?? []).map((ap) => {
  const was = prevAccessById.get(ap.id);
  return {
    ...ap,
    accessOriginLevelId:
      ap.accessOriginLevelId ?? was?.accessOriginLevelId ?? (was ? undefined : prev.level_id),
    createdAt: keep(ap.createdAt ?? was?.createdAt, !prevAccessIds.has(ap.id)),
  };
}),

Only a marker this floor has never seen is stamped. A generated copy already carries the origin it was cloned from (the spread in withAccessSpan preserves it), so it is left alone — re-stamping would make every floor its own origin, which is every member claiming to be the parent. Markers already in prev without an origin are pre-#666 data and stay unstamped, resolving exactly as they do today.

One field, one call site. accessParent, accessDirections, isAccessChild, the two cards and the routing side all read it unchanged.

Tests

src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/bridge.test.ts

  • stamps the origin level onto a marker this floor has never seen — the proof. Reverting the bridge change fails this test and only this test.
  • leaves a generated copy's origin alone on the floor it landed on
  • does not backfill an origin onto markers prev already held

src/lib/editor/__tests__/access.test.ts

  • keeps the drawn marker as parent after it connects floors below — the reported flow end to end: marker on L3, span down to L1/L2, parent stays drawn and accessDirections reads { down: [L2, L1], up: [] }.
  • cannot identify the drawn marker from timestamps alone — pins why the origin carries this and not createdAt: it asserts the copy inherits createdAt: 100 and that accessParent therefore picks the wrong member. Guards the fix against being "simplified" back into rule 2.

Acceptance

  • A Lift drawn on an upper floor stays the parent after Downstairs is set.
  • The parent card keeps Type / Downstairs / Upstairs; the generated copies show the child card.
  • View parent from a child navigates to the floor the marker was drawn on.
  • The Not linked badge appears on the drawn marker, not on a generated copy.
  • Existing projects resolve their parents exactly as before — no backfill, no re-parenting on load.
  • tsc --noEmit, eslint, vitest green.

Manual verification

  1. Multi-floor project → Access tool → place a Lift on Level 3.
  2. Selection card → Down lift → tick Level 2 and Level 1.
  3. The Level 3 card still shows Type / Down lift / Up lift. It does not turn into "Managed by parent".
  4. Go to Level 1, select the copy → child card → View parent returns to Level 3.
  5. Map mode: Not linked shows once, on Level 3.
  6. Open a project created before this change → parents resolve as they did; nothing re-parents.

Out of scope

issues.display_title: Issue #680: Wizard Add More Floors: re-importing the same Mappedin ZIP stages duplicate level ids
issues.main_description_html:
Importing the same Mappedin ZIP twice through wizard step 2's Add More Floors stages two levels with the same level_id and two floor configs with the same id.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Repro

  1. Wizard step 2 → import a Mappedin ZIP → review modal → Add More Floors
  2. Import the same ZIP again → Add More Floors
  3. The project now holds each imported level twice under the same id

Two ZIPs from different venues do not collide — Mappedin ids are venue-scoped — so this needs the same file (or two exports of the same venue) to bite.

Where

src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:196-210 merges into the live store while asking the merge to keep the file's ids:

const staged = mergeImportIntoProject({
  groups,
  levels: importSource.canvasData.levels,
  canvasData: store.canvasData,     // ← already holds the first import
  floorConfigs: store.floorConfigs,
  keepIds: true,
  prepend: true,
});

src/lib/mappedin-import/mergeIntoProject.ts:87 takes it at its word, with no check against what is already there:

const levelId = keepIds ? floor.id : newId();

The keepIds doc comment (mergeIntoProject.ts:22-27) justifies itself with "the import IS the project: nothing can collide". That holds for Continue to Editor (StepUploadFloor.tsx:146-152 passes canvasData: { ...src.canvasData, levels: [] } and floorConfigs: [] — an empty target) and does not hold for Add More Floors.

The obvious fix is wrong

Dropping keepIds from the Add More Floors call alone breaks the Uploaded list. handleRemoveImportedFloor (StepUploadFloor.tsx:237-249) unstages by the id the UI holds:

setFloorConfigs(store.floorConfigs.filter((f) => f.id !== id));
if (base) setCanvasData({ ...base, levels: base.levels.filter((l) => l.level_id !== id) });

and the ids the UI holds come from importedGroups, which is built from groupFloorsByBuilding(importResult) — i.e. the file's floor ids. Mint new ids in the merge and the remove button silently stops removing anything, because store ids no longer match the ones the list is keyed by.

So keepIds: true on this path is load-bearing, not an oversight. Whatever the fix is, the Uploaded list and the store have to end up agreeing on one set of ids.

Two shapes that would work

Pick whichever is smaller once you are in the code — both are fine, this is not a decision that needs making up front:

  1. Collide-aware ids in the merge. When keepIds is on, fall back to a fresh id for any floor whose id already exists in the target, and return the id mapping so the caller can restamp importedGroups. Keeps the UI keyed by whatever actually landed.
  2. Stage first, then derive the list. Let the merge always mint ids for this path and rebuild importedGroups from staged.floorConfigs instead of from importResult, so the list is downstream of the store rather than parallel to it.

Not in scope: Continue to Editor's keepIds (its target is empty by construction), and the information/category staging below it — Information carries no level id, and those records are already de-duplicated by their own id at StepUploadFloor.tsx:216-228.

Acceptance

  • Importing the same ZIP twice via Add More Floors produces distinct level_ids and distinct floorConfig.ids
  • Both copies appear in the Uploaded list, and removing one removes exactly that one from the list and from the store
  • Continue to Editor is unchanged — imported ids still match the staged Information records
  • Existing uploads and previously imported floors are untouched
  • A case in src/lib/mappedin-import/__tests__/mergeIntoProject.test.ts covers merging a group whose ids already exist in the target
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Found while validating PRD #633 against the code — the grouping feature itself is already shipped (#643 → #662), this is the one real defect the audit turned up.

RESULT

Branch: feature/680-import-duplicate-level-ids (from development) · Commit: dbfa496

Fix

keepIds is now a preference, not a promise. A floor whose id is already taken in the target gets a fresh one:

const levelId = keepIds && !taken.has(floor.id) ? floor.id : newId();
taken.add(levelId);
idMap.set(floor.id, levelId);

taken is seeded from the target's level ids and its floor config ids — configs are keyed by level id, so a duplicate there breaks the floor list just as badly — and grows as the merge hands ids out, so a file that lists the same floor twice cannot collide with itself either.

Continue to Editor is unaffected. Its target is empty by construction (canvasData: { ...src.canvasData, levels: [] }, floorConfigs: []), so every id it asks for is free and the review modal still predicts the project exactly. Covered by a regression test.

Why not just drop keepIds at the call site

That was the smaller diff and the wrong one. importedGroups — the Uploaded list — is built from the import, and handleRemoveImportedFloor (StepUploadFloor.tsx:237-249) filters the store by the ids that list holds. Minting ids the list never learns about leaves a remove button that quietly removes nothing.

So the merge reports where each floor landed, and the caller restamps:

setImportedGroups((prev) => [
  ...groups.map((g) => ({
    ...g,
    floors: g.floors.map((f) => ({ ...f, id: staged.idMap.get(f.id) ?? f.id })),
  })),
  ...prev,
]);

The setImportedGroups call also moved to after the merge, since it now depends on its result.

Re-keying is safe

Checked before writing it: nothing persisted in canvasData references a level by id. level_id appears exactly once in useMapStore.types.ts (on LevelData itself); doors hang off wallId; Information links through area.infoId and carries no level id. Every other levelId in the codebase is ephemeral — collab presence, runtime params, snap matches. A re-keyed level takes nothing with it.

Files

 src/lib/mappedin-import/mergeIntoProject.ts             | +19 −4
 src/lib/mappedin-import/__tests__/mergeIntoProject.test.ts | +88
 src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx                | +14 −5

Checks

pnpm test 142 files, 1165 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed · pnpm lint clean · tsc --noEmit clean.

Baseline on clean development is 1161 passed, so the delta is exactly the four tests added.

Three of the four were confirmed to fail with the guard reverted:

  • mints a fresh id for an imported floor whose id the project already holds — FAILS without
  • reports where every imported floor landed — FAILS without
  • does not let one import collide with itself when a file lists a floor twice — FAILS without
  • still keeps the file's ids when the target is empty — passes either way by design; it is the regression guard for Continue to Editor

Not covered by automation

The acceptance item "removing one removes exactly that one from the list and from the store" is the reason for the idMap restamp, but there is no component test for StepUploadFloor — the file has none today and standing one up needs the whole wizard store plus file-picker plumbing. Worth one manual pass: import a ZIP → Add More Floors → import the same ZIP → remove one of the second copy's floors → confirm exactly that floor leaves both the Uploaded list and the staged project.

Demo

.playwright-mcp/demo/680/video-680-duplicate-import-ids.mp4 — 1920×1080, 60 fps, 71.8 s, recorded against a production build (pnpm build + the standalone server) in an isolated worktree, not next dev.

The scenario drives the real wizard: new project → Manual Coordinates on the fixture's venue → step 2 → import mappedin-two-buildings.zip → Add More Floors → import the same file again → Add More Floors.

It proves the fix without ever showing an id, because the id is what the Remove button filters by:

After removing one floor 5 floors — only that row went, and its twin in the other copy is still there

Before this commit that last number was 4: both copies shared one id, so one click filtered both out of the staged project.

Every count is asserted inside the scenario, not just narrated — it throws if the screen disagrees, so a recording that completes is a passing test.

Need Already here
DOM handles over MapLibre, reprojected on move/zoom/pitch src/components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx — the same overlay, already draggable via onMovePoint
Map position → active-floor model px lngLatToLevelPixel() src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:429; its doc comment says any consumer that WRITES a px position picked on the map must invert through this, not lngLatToPixel
Live drag without spamming undo setCanvasDataSilent src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts:241, commit with history via setCanvasData :198 — exactly how the building drag already works (Editor3DMapView.tsx:240-241)

No-walls state Editor3DMapView.tsx:360-372 already renders "This level has no walls to preview in 3D."

So nothing new is needed in the store beyond the mode flag. #681 §3 asks for a new live+commit wall action; movePoint (editorSlice.ts:463) is the closest precedent but it pushes no history entry at all — routing the drag through the existing silent/commit pair gives one undo entry per drag for free and keeps a single history code path.

Scope

  1. State — mapWallEditMode: boolean + setMapWallEditMode(on) in src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts. Ephemeral: not persisted, not part of canvasHistory, default false, forced off when leaving Map mode or unmounting Editor3DMapView, never settable without edit permission.
  2. Geometry helpers — src/lib/map/wall-vertex-edit.ts:
    • wallVertexHandles(level) → { id, wallId, pointIndex, x, y }[] for the active level.
    • previousFloorInBuilding(canvasData, activeLevelId) → nearest lower floor inside the same building group (the snap task consumes it; land it here with its test).
    • Pure functions, tests in src/lib/map/__tests__/wall-vertex-edit.test.ts.
  3. Overlay — src/components/editor/map-wall-edit/MapWallVertexHandles.tsx. Project each handle through computeCoordSpace + makeLevelPixelTransform + pixelToLngLat + levelBaseHeights like MapObjectMarkers does, reposition on render/move/zoom/pitch/rotate, hide handles that are off-screen or not projectable, compact draggable buttons with real hover/focus/drag states.

  5. Toolbar — toggle in EditorBottomToolbar.tsx inside the existing canEdit block. Title Edit wall points, aria-pressed reflects the mode, mutually exclusive with mapMoveMode (Drag building) in both directions, and visually separate from the placement group (MapScopeButton / MapTransformButton) so it never reads as a placement tool.

Decide these on purpose, not by accident

  1. WallLayer.points is a polyline (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:41-52), not always two points. Handle every vertex by its index — the PRD's "endpoint" is only the 2-point case.
  2. Curved walls carry h1x/h1y/h2x/h2y. Moving a vertex leaves the bezier handles pointing at the old position. PRD non-goal 3 rules out curve editing, so hide handles on walls that have curve handles set rather than silently deforming them.
  3. Only the dragged vertex moves even when another wall ends on the same coordinate (R10): match on wall id + point index, never on coordinate.
  4. Wall geometry is editor data, not placement. The drag must leave level.mapTransform, building.mapTransform and the project offset untouched.

  • A drag updates canvasData.levels[].layout.walls[].points live, and the moved point is there after switching to the 2D Editor
  • One completed drag = one undo entry; Undo restores the pre-drag position and does not step through drag frames
  • A press on a handle never starts a map pan, a building drag, or a feature selection
  • A wall sharing that coordinate does not move
  • Floor, building and project transforms are unchanged after a drag
  • Active floor with no walls → no handles, existing message still shown

issues.display_title: Issue #689: Editor Map: snap wall vertex drags to the previous floor, with an override key (PRD #681)
issues.main_description_html:
While a wall vertex is dragged in Map mode, it should snap to the floor below — that is the whole point of correcting geometry in the 3D view instead of the 2D Editor — with a key to drag freely when the target genuinely is not on the floor below.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From PRD #681 — R15–R18. Builds on #688 (the mode, the handles and the drag write path); that one lands previousFloorInBuilding(), this one uses it.

What is already in the repo

  • src/lib/map/floorSnap.ts snaps a floor's footprint bbox to its neighbours — center/min/max per axis (#594). Different problem: it never looks at a vertex, so the geometry here is new. Copy its shape, not its math: pure module, everything passed in, no store/map/DOM reads, so drag and tests cannot drift.
  • src/lib/map/useSnapGuideLayer.ts (SNAP_GUIDE_SOURCE / SNAP_GUIDE_LAYER) already renders snap feedback as a map line and takes matches as input — the feedback surface exists, and Editor3DMapView.tsx:251-259 shows how it is wired.
  • previousFloorInBuilding() in src/lib/map/wall-vertex-edit.ts resolves the reference floor; groupLevelsByBuilding() (geojson-utils.ts:860) is what makes it per-building.

Scope

  1. snapWallVertex(point, targets, options) in src/lib/map/wall-vertex-edit.ts → snapped point + what it caught (or free).
  2. Target extraction from the previous floor's walls: every vertex, plus the nearest point on each wall segment.
  3. Vertex beats segment when both are in range — a corner is what the user is aiming at.
  4. Alt held (or equivalent) = free drag, no snap, no snap state. Held state read at drag time, not at drag start, so it can be pressed mid-drag.
  5. Snap feedback while snapped: changed dot state, plus a guide/highlight of the caught target.
  6. No previous floor in the building → free drag and no snap affordance at all; the mode still works.

Decide these on purpose

issues.display_title: Issue #696: Analytics: integrate Countly Web SDK (countly-sdk-web) reporting to https://data.gothru.org
issues.main_description_html:
Wire the Countly Web SDK into the frontend so sessions, page views, and JS errors are reported to the self-hosted Countly server at https://data.gothru.org.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Current state — what the repo does and does not have

Fact Where
No analytics of any kind today grep for countly/gtag/posthog/mixpanel is empty
The one global client mount point src/app/providers.tsx ("use client", wraps every route from src/app/layout.tsx)
CSP connect-src is a strict allow-list next.config.ts — 'self' + maplibre / openfreemap / gothru.co / arcgis, plus collabCsp derived at build time from NEXT_PUBLIC_COLLAB_URL
Public env var convention NEXT_PUBLIC_*, documented in .env.example, real values in untracked .env.local

The CSP is the part that will silently break this. Every Countly request goes out as XMLHttpRequest (node_modules/countly-sdk-web/lib/countly.js:6721) — there is no image beacon and no injected <script> on the paths we use, so adding the Countly origin to connect-src is both necessary and sufficient. The createElement("iframe") / createElement("script") paths inside the SDK belong to the feedback-widget and boomerang APM plugins, which this task does not enable — so frame-src, script-src, and img-src stay untouched.

Scope

  1. Dependency — countly-sdk-web (26.1.3). Ships its own lib/countly.d.ts, no @types package needed.
  2. src/lib/analytics/countly.ts — a lazy singleton that import()s the SDK on first use, calls Countly.init({ app_key, url }) exactly once, and turns on track_sessions() + track_errors(). Returns null when there is no app key or no window, so every call site degrades to a no-op.
  3. src/components/analytics/CountlyAnalytics.tsx — "use client", renders null, reports track_pageview(pathname) on every App Router navigation via usePathname().
  4. Mount — inside Providers so it covers every route, including /embed and the public /v/[key] viewer.
  5. CSP — derive the Countly origin from NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_URL in next.config.ts the same way collabCsp is derived, and append it to connect-src.
  6. .env.example — document NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_APP_KEY.
  7. Test — src/lib/analytics/__tests__/countly.test.ts: no app key ⇒ no SDK load and no init; app key ⇒ init called once across repeated calls.

Decisions made on purpose

  • Dynamic import() inside an effect, not a static import. The SDK touches window/localStorage; a static import puts it in the server bundle and in the initial client chunk for a payload nobody needs before hydration.
  • No app key ⇒ the SDK is never even downloaded. That is the dev/CI default, so no local session ever pollutes production data.
  • usePathname() only, not useSearchParams(). useSearchParams forces a Suspense boundary or a full client-render bailout on every page that mounts it — too high a price for query strings in a view name. Countly still records the full URL itself.
  • No consent gating (require_consent) for now. Add it when the cookie/consent banner exists; wiring an always-granted consent call today is dead code.
  • The app key is not committed. It goes in .env.local on dev and in /home/config on the prod host.

Acceptance criteria

  • With NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_APP_KEY set, loading any page produces begin_session + a view request to https://data.gothru.org/i with HTTP 200, and no CSP violation in the console.
  • Client-side navigation (e.g. dashboard → editor) reports a new view without a full page load.
  • With the app key unset, countly-sdk-web is never fetched and nothing is logged or thrown.
  • No window is not defined during pnpm build / SSR.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit all green.

RESULT

Countly Web SDK is wired in and merged to development and main.

issues.display_title: Issue #697: fix(analytics): stop sending public share keys to Countly, and double-reporting views under StrictMode
issues.main_description_html:
Two defects in the Countly view reporting shipped by #696, both in the same file. Neither is hypothetical: the app key is now set, so both are affecting live data.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

1. The public share key is being sent to Countly

src/components/analytics/CountlyAnalytics.tsx:20 reports track_pageview(pathname), and on the public viewer the pathname is the share key — /v/ab12cd34. That key is the access credential for a customer's published indoor map (src/lib/preview/publish.ts:25); anyone who can open the Countly dashboard can read a list of every published map and open them. /embed/[key] has the same shape, and /editor/[projectId] and /preview/[projectId] leak project UUIDs.

It is also a data-quality problem on its own: Countly writes one app_viewsmeta document per distinct view name, so the Views report becomes an unbounded list of one-hit keys and the aggregate question — how many editor sessions, how many public-viewer opens — cannot be read off the dashboard at all. /v and /embed are the highest-traffic routes, so they dominate the noise.

Note that the SDK stamps a second field, view, from Countly.getViewUrl() (node_modules/countly-sdk-web/lib/countly.js:7913), which returns window.location.pathname — so passing a normalised name to track_pageview is not enough on its own. getViewUrl is an overridable namespace function (countly.d.ts:576); override it too, or the raw key still leaves the browser on every view.

Fix: normalise dynamic segments before reporting, and override getViewUrl to the same normalised value.

Route Reported as
/v/<key> /v/[key]
/embed/<key> /embed/[key]
/editor/<uuid> /editor/[projectId]
/preview/<uuid> /preview/[projectId]

2. StrictMode reports every dev page view twice

src/components/analytics/CountlyAnalytics.tsx:19 has no double-invoke guard. next.config.ts sets no reactStrictMode, and Next defaults __NEXT_STRICT_MODE_APP to true, so the dev server mounts → unmounts → remounts the component and the effect body runs twice for the same pathname. The memoised promise in countly() dedupes init(), not the .then callbacks.

Reproduced against the real SDK: two back-to-back track_pageview("/editor/abc") calls queue [CLY]_view {visit:1, start:1}, then a spurious [CLY]_view {dur:0} closing it after zero seconds, then a second {visit:1} with a fresh view id. Root cause is in the SDK — track_pageview calls reportViewDuration() unconditionally (countly.js:3956) and has no same-name dedupe.

Dev-only (StrictMode double-invokes effects only in React dev builds), but .env.local now carries a real app key pointing at the same Countly app as production, so every dev page load adds 2 visits and drags the average view duration toward 0.

Fix: guard on the last reported view name with a ref — refs survive StrictMode's simulated remount, and a real navigation still reports because the value differs.

Acceptance criteria

  • A page load in pnpm dev produces exactly one [CLY]_view, with no dur:0 closer.
  • Opening a published map reports the view name /v/[key], and the event's view field is /v/[key] too — the raw key appears in neither.
  • Static routes (/, /dashboard, /login) are unchanged.
  • Unit test covers the normaliser table above and the StrictMode double-mount.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Both defects fixed and merged to development via #704.

1. Share key / project id no longer leave the browser. normalizeViewPath() in src/lib/analytics/countly.ts collapses /v/<key> → /v/[key], /embed/<key> → /embed/[key], /editor/<uuid> → /editor/[projectId], /preview/<uuid> → /preview/[projectId]. The pattern is deliberately unanchored at the end, so any deeper path under those prefixes collapses to the same template rather than leaking a segment nobody anticipated.

As the issue predicted, normalising the name passed to track_pageview was not sufficient on its own — the SDK stamps a second URL field from getViewUrl() (countly.js:7913), which returns window.location.pathname verbatim. getViewUrl is now overridden to the same normaliser, and the override is installed before init() so it is in place ahead of the first view.

2. StrictMode double-report fixed. src/components/analytics/CountlyAnalytics.tsx guards on a useRef holding the last reported pathname. The comparison deliberately uses the raw pathname, not the normalised name: comparing the normalised value would have made a real navigation between two projects report only once, since both collapse to /editor/[projectId].

  • src/components/analytics/__tests__/CountlyAnalytics.test.tsx — 3 cases rendered inside a real <StrictMode>: one view per mount despite the double invoke, the route template rather than the share key on the public viewer, and two reports when the user moves between two projects.

The tests were checked against a broken implementation, not just run green. With the ref guard removed, all three component tests fail with expected 1 times, but got 2 times — so the StrictMode double-invoke is genuinely reproduced under vitest rather than passing vacuously.

issues.display_title: Issue #698: Analytics: wizard funnel events + shared trackEvent helper (Countly)
issues.main_description_html:
Instrument the setup wizard funnel with Countly custom events, and add the small shared helper the rest of the analytics work will build on. From the event inventory run against #696.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Why this one first

All four wizard steps render at the same URL (/start), so CountlyAnalytics.tsx fires exactly one view for the entire wizard. The product's most important funnel — how many visitors reach a finished project, and which step they abandon — is currently invisible, and no amount of view tracking will fix it.

Shared helper (lands here, used by every later analytics task)

A thin wrapper over countly() in src/lib/analytics/, so call sites read as one line and the event keys live in one place. Nothing elaborate: a trackEvent(key, { segmentation, count, sum, dur }) that no-ops when the SDK is off, plus the key union type. Server actions cannot call it — the SDK is browser-only — so every event below fires from the client caller, not from src/actions/.

Events

wizard_step_entered

  • Call site: src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts:248, inside the existing useMapStore.subscribe((state, prev) => ...) registered by the effect at :244. It already discriminates step transitions at :251 and :276, so prev is handed to you.
  • Not WizardShell.tsx — and this is load-bearing, not a style call. React runs child effects before parent effects; StartPage (src/app/start/page.tsx:7) calls useWizardPersistence and then renders WizardShell, and the synchronous restoreFromLocal() → hydratePersistedState → setCurrentSetupStep(lastVisited) (src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:194) runs in the parent's effect. A WizardShell effect always observes step 0 first, so a resumed wizard would be reported as a real 0→2 forward walk and silently inflate the funnel.
  • Guard, required: the same hook is mounted by src/app/editor/[projectId]/page.tsx:17, and wizardState.ts:194 mutates currentSetupStep on every editor open. Without if (projectId) return; every editor load emits phantom wizard steps. The effect at :244 already closes over projectId (used at :235).
  • Segmentation: step: 0_location | 1_floors | 2_order | 3_generate (index-prefixed so Countly's alphabetical value dropdown reads in wizard order) · direction: enter | forward | back (enter from a one-shot mount emit; an enter with step > 0_location is the resume signal) · max_step_reached: 0|1|2|3 from lastVisitedStep (src/store/mapStore/wizardSlice.ts:8).
  • Fire on entry, not as a timed event. start_event/end_event only send on end_event, so the step a user abandons never reports — precisely the one you need.

wizard_location_confirmed

  • Call site: src/components/setup/StepSelectLocation.tsx:138 (handleConfirm) — after the await at :143-153, and in the catch at :154.
  • Segmentation: result: created | reused | failed · coord_mode: pin | manual · address_present: bool.
  • Never send the raw failure text — :155 surfaces err.message straight from the Go API.

floor_plan_upload

  • Call site: src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:104 (xhr.onload success) and the shared fail helper at :71, which already covers HTTP non-2xx (:90), bad body (:107) and network error (:110). Client-side rejections happen before any request: :263 (unsupported MIME), :267 (over MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB).
  • Segmentation: result: success | http_error | bad_response | network_error | rejected_format | rejected_size | no_project · mime (raw file.type, "unknown" when the browser gives "") · ext (lowercased, derived from the name) · size_mb: <1 | 1-5 | 5-10 | >10 · batch_size: 1 | 2-5 | 6-20 | 20+ · status (only when result=http_error).
  • Worth having because a failed upload leaves the user stuck: Continue stays disabled until every file has a serverPath.

wizard_completed

  • Call site: src/lib/wizard/completeWizard.ts:24, before the localStorage wipe. Four callers funnel through it: StepGenerate.tsx:87 and :95, StepUploadFloor.tsx:184, useWizardPersistence.ts:289.
  • Segmentation: exit: generated | blank_canvas | import · floors (count) · no_project: bool.
  • completeWizard is a plain module but browser-only anyway because of its localStorage write, so countly() is safe there even though the updateProject it calls on :25 is a server action.

project_start_method

  • Call site: src/components/projects/NewProjectFlow.tsx:169 (ChoiceCard variant="scan"); the competing branch is :170 (empty canvas, which creates a project directly at :123-131 and never enters the wizard).
  • Segmentation: method: scan_floor_plan | empty_canvas · source: dashboard | editor_file_menu.

PII rules for this task

Never segment on: location.address, location.lat/lng (wizardSlice.ts:9, rendered at 6 decimal places in StepSelectLocation.tsx:42-43 — that pinpoints a building), projectName (routinely a client's company name), projectId, and anything from uploadedFiles — file.name and the returned serverPath are a customer filename and a raw storage key.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every event above appears in Countly with the exact keys and bounded values listed; no free text, no ids.
  • Walking the wizard end to end produces one wizard_step_entered per transition and exactly one wizard_completed.
  • Opening the editor produces zero wizard events.
  • A resumed wizard reports direction=enter at its restored step, not a forward walk from 0.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

All five events plus the shared helper are in, merged to development via #705.

File What landed
src/lib/analytics/events.ts trackEvent(key, payload) over countly(), with AnalyticsEvent as a union so a typo is a type error. Plus the bucket helpers every later task will reuse: sizeBucketMb, countBucket, fileExtension, wizardStepLabel.
src/lib/analytics/uploadEvent.ts reportUpload() — the upload has six outcomes across three call sites and the segmentation has to be identical at all of them.
src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts wizard_step_entered from the existing store subscriber, plus a one-shot mount emit above it.
src/components/setup/StepSelectLocation.tsx wizard_location_confirmed.
src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx floor_plan_upload, wired through fail() so every failure path is covered by one change.
src/lib/wizard/completeWizard.ts wizard_completed, plus the new WizardExit type; the four callers pass their exit and floor count.
src/components/projects/NewProjectFlow.tsx project_start_method.

Everything the issue asked for was confirmed against the tree

  • The WizardShell ordering hazard is real, and the report lives in the hook's subscriber instead. Covered by a test that pre-sets step 2 before mount and asserts the entry reports 2_order, not a walk from 0.
  • The editor guard is in and tested: mounting the hook with a projectId and then moving currentSetupStep emits nothing.
  • Fires on entry, not as a timed event.
  • source on NewProjectFlow really was dead — declared on Props, passed by both call sites, never destructured. Now used.

Two things the issue did not anticipate

  1. projectId had to join the subscriber effect's dependency array. It was [disabled] and did not reference the prop before; now it does, and react-hooks/exhaustive-deps flagged it. A stale value there is exactly the phantom-editor-steps bug the guard exists to prevent.
  2. wizard_completed needed per-project deduplication. The generate path reaches completeWizard twice — the store subscriber latches the project complete the moment the twin appears (useWizardPersistence.ts), then the user presses Open Editor (StepGenerate.tsx). Without the guard every generated project counted as two finished wizards.

Behaviour note

An upload returning 2xx with no serverPath is now reported as bad_response rather than success. That state leaves the row looking finished while Continue stays disabled. No app behaviour changed — only the reporting is honest about it.

Tests

  • src/lib/analytics/__tests__/events.test.ts — 18 cases: payload shape, count default and override, and every bucket boundary.
  • src/hooks/__tests__/useWizardPersistence.funnel.test.tsx — 4 cases: entry under a real <StrictMode> wrapper, the resumed-step case, forward/back directions, and silence in the editor.
  • src/lib/wizard/__tests__/completeWizard.test.ts — 4 added cases: exit and floor count, the no-project case, the duplicate-completion dedupe, and silence when no analytics argument is passed.

Checked against a broken implementation, not just run green: removing the entry-report ref guard makes the StrictMode test fail with expected [2 items] to deeply equal [1 item].

Privacy

No address, coordinate, project name, floor name, file name, server path, or raw error string is reported. Only bounded labels, buckets, and counts.

Verification

  • Segmentation: surface: wizard_generate | editor_add_floor · outcome: success | no_file | http_error | stream_error | stream_ended · wall_source: net | cv · wall_threshold: default | custom (default is 0.5 at StepGenerate.tsx:56 and useAddLevel.ts:35) · attempt: first | retry_floor | retry_all.

  • Duration: add_event({ dur }) from a performance.now() delta. Not start_event/end_event — concurrent floors would clobber the keyed timer.

floor_plan_scan_run — one per Generate press

issues.main_description_html:
Instrument the editor — which tools get used, whether levels get added, and whether saving is quietly failing. From the event inventory run against #696. Depends on the trackEvent helper landing in the wizard-funnel task.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Events

editor_tool_selected

  • Call sites: src/components/editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx:292 (all 2D tools, toolbar and keyboard alike), the Shapes dropdown at :737, and src/components/editor/EditorBottomToolbar.tsx:42/:43/:94 for the map surface. Fire only when the mode value is non-null.
  • Do not instrument FloorplanEditor.tsx:752 — the access dropdown already emits mode("access") via index.ts:142 and would double-count.
  • Segmentation: tool: wall | curveWall | door | window | area | point | safety | access | shape_rect | shape_circle | shape_polygon | select | drag_building | wall_vertex · surface: floorplan | map · via: toolbar | keyboard.
  • The single biggest unknown in the product: roughly 14 tools ship and nobody knows which are reached for. This is the highest-volume event in the editor, so no ids in segmentation — nanoid level/building values would blow up Countly's cardinality.

floor_plan_save_failed

  • Call site: src/components/editor/EditorTopbar.tsx:122.
  • Segmentation: stage: update_project | save_floorplan | unknown (not derivable from failureMessage — set a stage variable before each await, i.e. before :101 and before :111) · trigger: autosave | unmount_flush | manual (pass as a saveNow(trigger) argument so :151, the timer, is distinguishable from :141, the unmount flush) · reason: unauthorized | forbidden | server | network | unknown.
  • unauthorized is the exact string saveFloorplanAction returns when there is no access token (src/actions/projects.ts:272) and is the most valuable bucket here.
  • Autosave is the product's data-durability promise and its failure is invisible today — the catch writes a message and nothing else. A user can lose an editing session and we would never know.

level_added

  • Call site: src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:196 — turn it into addFloorOnce(source) firing after the dedupe guard at :197, with "blank" from :218 and "ai_scan" from :247.
  • Segmentation: source: blank | ai_scan | txt_import | txt_drop_empty | mappedin_import · into_existing_building: true | false (from selectedBuildingId != null; omit the key entirely on mappedin_import). Level count goes in count: 1 for the four single-level paths, merged.floorConfigs.length - store.floorConfigs.length for the import.
  • Levels are the unit of work in indoor mapping and there are four completely different ways to get one, which is exactly the split worth seeing.

panorama_import

  • Call site: src/components/editor/floorplan-editor/AddPanoramaButton.tsx:53.
  • Segmentation: outcome: imported | no_panoramas | lookup_failed · error_code: input_invalid | tour_not_found | load_failed (only on lookup_failed, from AddPanoramaModal.tsx:274-276) · alignment_applied: bool (the 4th arg of onImported, currently discarded as _viaAlignment) · had_positions: bool (the canAlign expression already computed at AddPanoramaModal.tsx:55). Panorama count goes in sum.
  • Panorama placement is how a floor plan becomes a walkable digital twin.

PII rules for this task

Never send the floor name (useAddLevel.ts:199 — free user text, and on imports it comes straight out of a customer's file), file.name, serverPath, raw error strings (res.error is server text that can carry ids or paths), tour.tourKey or the pasted tour URL (AddPanoramaModal.tsx:250), or any projectId/levelId.

Explicitly out of scope

No event per save. The editor autosaves 2 seconds after every change; an event there would dwarf everything else in the app. The "how much mapping actually got done" question is answered by a single summary event on leave, which is tracked separately in the phase-2 task.

Acceptance criteria

  • Selecting each tool once, by toolbar and by keyboard, produces one event per selection with the right via, and the access dropdown produces exactly one — not two.
  • Forcing a save failure (revoke the token) produces floor_plan_save_failed with reason=unauthorized and the correct trigger.
  • Adding a level by each of the five sources reports the matching source.
  • No id, filename, or free-text name appears in any segmentation value.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

All four events are in, merged to development via #707. New reporters: src/lib/analytics/toolEvent.ts, saveEvent.ts, levelEvent.ts, panoramaEvent.ts.

Five things in this issue were wrong against the current tree

Stated Actual
the access dropdown emits via index.ts:142 :140. The claim is correct, the line is not — :142 is a comment inside the setShapeTool doc block. Verified chain: index.ts:140 → commands.ts:69 setAddMode → :54 applyAdd → :58 ctx.on.mode(ctx.addKind), all synchronous. FloorplanEditor.tsx:752 is correctly left uninstrumented.
a saveNow(trigger) argument covers all three triggers It cannot. The Save button never goes through saveNow — handleSave calls saveFloorplanAction directly — so manual needed its own two reports. handleSave's signature was deliberately not changed: onClick={handleSave} would pass the React MouseEvent as the first argument.
panorama_import carries lookup_failed, no_panoramas and error_code All three are structurally unreachable. onImported is only called from commit(), which bails unless the modal state is loaded, and the Import buttons only render when panoramas.length > 0. The lookup is already covered end to end by virtual_tour_load (#699). Keeping them would have double-reported the same thing under two keys.
_viaAlignment is the 4th arg and is discarded It is the 3rd; the 4th, positions, is used.
line numbers in useAddLevel.ts and AddPanoramaModal.tsx All shifted by #699.

What the events ended up as

  • editor_tool_selected — tool (14 closed values) · surface (editor_2d / map) · source (toolbar / keyboard). Reported from the engine's mode callback for the 8 engine tools, directly from the Shapes dropdown for the 3 shapes, and from the three map handlers.
  • floor_plan_save_failed — stage · trigger · reason · status · role. Three report sites: the saveNow catch, and both failure exits of handleSave.
  • level_added — source (5 values) · into_existing_building (omitted for imports) · Countly count (36 for a 36-floor import, not 36 events).
  • panorama_import — outcome (imported / no_level / no_canvas) · alignment_applied · any_aligned · had_positions · dropped · count_bucket (conditional) · sum = panoramas placed.

What made the naive edit wrong

  1. The mode callback fires with null constantly — every mount, floor switch, file load and remote collab apply, plus Escape and the deselect re-click. toolForMode returns undefined for anything unmapped and the report is skipped; otherwise null would be the highest-volume value in the event.
  2. Toolbar and keyboard are indistinguishable at that callback — applyAdd has no origin argument. A ref raised immediately before the engine call and reset on every callback entry recovers it, safe only because the callback fires synchronously inside setAddMode. The access dropdown bypasses setAddMode, so it raises the flag without reporting.
  3. Shapes are the mirror image — setShapeTool clears addKind first, so the engine only ever emits mode(null) for them; they report from the dropdown row.
  4. level_added sits inside addFloorOnce, below the dedupe guard. In handleAddAndScanFloor instead, every Retry Scan would count a second level.
  5. caps.role is read through a ref. In saveNow's dependency array it would change the callback's identity when the role resolves, and the unmount-flush effect depends on saveNow — every role resolution would fire an extra save labelled unmount_flush. react-hooks/refs also rejects a ref write during render, so it lives in an effect.
  6. The map toggles report only their ON transition, and Drag is guarded on !mapMoveMode.

Known caveat, deliberately not fixed

The unmount-flush effect has deps [caps.canEdit, saveNow], and canEdit starts false and flips true once the role resolves, so its cleanup runs while the component is still mounted. Pre-existing behaviour, but those saves now carry trigger: unmount_flush — so that value is not perfectly trustworthy. Fixing it changes when saves happen, which is outside this task.

Also noted: EditorBottomToolbar and EditorTopbar are both rendered by src/app/design-preview/collaboration/CollaborationPreview.tsx, which seeds the store for real. Interacting with that internal page emits real events. Low volume, not gated.

Tests

src/lib/analytics/__tests__/editorEvents.test.ts — 21 cases across the four reporters: the full toolForMode mapping and its rejection of null/""/unmapped values, the save reason buckets including offline vs unknown and a missing navigator, the import count and omitted building flag, and the panorama outcome/bucket/alignment logic.

Checked against broken implementations, not just run green. Making toolForMode fall back to "select" and making count_bucket unconditional (countBucket(0) returns "1", so a zero-placement import would report as a batch of one) each fail the suite; both were reverted.

Privacy

No id, file name, floor name, venue name, tour key, coordinate, email address or raw error string is reported. Three tests assert specifically that the owner email, the tour key and a venue-named file never reach a payload.

issues.display_title: Issue #702: Analytics: sign-in, sign-up, and email activation events (Countly)
issues.main_description_html:
Instrument authentication — sign-in, sign-up, and email activation. From the event inventory run against #696. Depends on the trackEvent helper landing in the wizard-funnel task.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Why

Nothing currently distinguishes a failed login from a bounce; only the /login view exists. And email verification is a hard gate — src/proxy.ts:43-49 redirects unverified users away from /start and /editor, so an account that never activates is an account that never reaches the product at all. That drop-off is invisible today.

Note that loginAction (src/actions/auth.ts:9) and registerAction (:31) are "use server" actions and cannot report — every event below fires from the client component that awaits them.

Events

sign_in

  • Call sites: src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx:40 (after await loginAction — success at :59, EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED at :43, generic failure at :50) and src/components/auth/GoogleSignInButton.tsx:46 (the signIn("google") redirect).
  • Segmentation: provider: credentials | google · outcome: success | invalid_credentials | email_not_verified | server_error | started | provider_error · surface: login | register.

sign_up

  • Call sites, all in src/app/(auth)/register/register-form.tsx: :67 (setCreated(true)) → created; :63, inside the if ("error" in result) block before the return → rejected_api; :55, the if (!passwordLongEnough) early return → rejected_password.
  • Segmentation: outcome: created | rejected_password | rejected_api. One key, three bounded values, no free text, no provider segment.

account_activation

  • Call sites: src/app/(auth)/verify-email/verify-email-client.tsx — one call inside the .then at :32-41, placed before the await update() on :39 so a failed session refresh cannot swallow the report, and one in the existing if (!token) return early return at :25-26 (not at :21, which is a useState initializer). Resend paths: src/app/(auth)/verify-email-pending/verify-pending-client.tsx:66 (sent), :59 (rate-limited), :63 (failed).
  • Segmentation: step: link_opened | resend_requested · outcome: verified | invalid_link | missing_token | sent | rate_limited | failed. Twelve combinations at most, no ids, no free text.

PII rules for this task — the strictest in the whole analytics effort

  • email and password are both in scope at login-form.tsx:40. fullName, email and password are locals at register-form.tsx:31-33, passed at :59. None of them may appear in any segmentation value, ever.
  • The activation token is a single-use credential and it is sitting in scope as token at verify-email-client.tsx:19. It must never reach Countly — not as a segment, not in an error string, not via the view name.
  • Never segment on result.error (register-form.tsx:62) — Go server text, unbounded, and it can echo the submitted email back.

Acceptance criteria

  • Each outcome above is reachable and reports the right bounded value — verify email_not_verified and rate_limited specifically, since they are the two that matter and the two easiest to miss.
  • No email, name, password, or token appears in any event payload. Check the actual network request, not just the code.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

All three events are in, merged to development via #711. New reporter: src/lib/analytics/authEvent.ts.

Event Where it fires
sign_in login-form.tsx — one call covering success and the three bucketed failures; GoogleSignInButton.tsx for started; a mount effect in login-form.tsx for provider_error
sign_up register-form.tsx — rejected_password at the length guard, rejected_api in the error branch, created after setCreated(true)
account_activation verify-email-client.tsx for link_opened (verified / invalid_link / missing_token); verify-pending-client.tsx for resend_requested (sent / rate_limited / failed)

Everything specified above was confirmed against the tree

All the cited line numbers and branches were real. Three things needed a decision the issue did not cover:

  1. Google needs both halves reported from different files. GoogleSignInButton hands the browser to Google with a full-page redirect and never regains control, so started is all it can observe. The failure returns as ?error= on the login page — that is where provider_error is reported, behind a ref so StrictMode's second effect pass does not double it.
  2. GoogleSignInButton gained a required surface prop. It is rendered on both /login and /register and had no way to say which. Both call sites updated; there are no others.
  3. Two placements are load-bearing. The verified report fires before await update(), so a failing session refresh cannot swallow the one signal that the account activated — exactly as the issue asked. The missing_token report uses its own ref rather than the existing single-use-token guard (ranRef), so it cannot block a token arriving on a later effect pass.

Privacy

The reporters take no free-text parameter at all. That is the guarantee rather than a convention: there is no argument through which a caller could pass an email, a full name, a password or the activation token. Every outcome is bucketed at the call site by comparing against a known literal — "EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED", "Invalid email or password", "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS" — and no backend string is ever forwarded, since those can echo the submitted address back. The activation token is a single-use credential and is never read into an event.
